Monte Carlo simulations of the colloidal epitaxy of hard spheres on a square pattern were performed.
The vertical system size was fixed at L_z = 200σ, which was large enough for the hard spheres to be randomly dispersed at the initial state.
The numbers of particles were N = 6656 and 26624, selected such that the number density on the bottom was the same as in previous simulations.
In some cases, the defect disappearance occurred at g* less than 0.9, while in others it occurred at g* greater than 0.9.
For the N = 26624 system, defect disappearance was observed in all three simulations, with two cases occurring during g* = 0.5-0.7.
In the N = 26624 system, an increase in disorder was observed at large g*.
Tetrahedral structures were often observed in the snapshots, suggesting the formation of stacking fault tetrahedra.
The evolution of the center of gravity was smooth and of a single relaxation mode when the defect disappearance occurred at lower g* than the flat bottom wall cases.
Temporal stopping of the sinking of the center of gravity was observed when the defect disappearance occurred at g* greater than 0.9 for the flat wall cases.
The authors noted that detailed analyses to observe the manner of defect disappearance and identify the structure of defects are left as future research.
The authors aim to systematically enlarge the system size and optimize the control of g* to efficiently erase defects in reality.
The use of a square pattern on the bottom substrate was an attempt to replace the artificial stress from the periodic boundary conditions in previous simulations.
The diagonal distance of the intersection of the longitudinal and transverse grooves on the square pattern was designed to coincide with the bottom (001) layer of the fcc crystal.
The separation between neighboring groove edges on the square pattern was 0.338σ, and the periodicity of the lattice was 1.045σ.
The authors observed the formation of a few crystalline layers at the bottom that matched the pattern on the lattice point, even at low g* values.
